Designed in Denmark, and meticulously assembled in Europe, the Norse Standard Loose LS T-shirt takes its inspiration from the 1940s crew neck t-shirt. These undershirts of the early-days were commonly made from cheap single cotton jersey, with a simple cut and sew construction and ribbed collar, making them easily accessible to produce for the mass consumer. The fit relaxed compared to its undergarment counterpart, as it was no longer necessary to fit snuggly beneath uniforms. The t-shirt’s versatility also lends itself as the ideal venue for a graphic, often used in military outfitting to depict a soldiers regiment.

The Burning Godzilla Selvedge is part of our official Godzilla® collaboration, this time inspired by one of the most iconic and volatile versions of the character, Burning Godzilla, from the 1995 film Godzilla vs. Destoroyah (ゴジラVSデストロイア).
In that film, Godzilla reaches a critical point. His heart functions like a nuclear reactor, and it’s in meltdown mode. His skin glows with radioactive heat, veins of fire running across his body, and his Heat Ray transforms into the devastating Burning Heat Ray (バーニング熱線 Bāningu Nessen). It’s one of the most striking designs in the franchise and one of the most emotionally charged endings in kaiju cinema.
The denim reflects that energy.
We used a super-heavy 20oz Japanese rope-dyed indigo selvedge, stiff and rich with texture. The interior weft glows in a deep, saturated orange-red, echoing the internal heat surging through Burning Godzilla’s body. The selvedge ID is metallic red, a nod to the concentrated blast of his final Heat Ray.
The fabric is woven in Japan on vintage shuttle looms and has a dry, structured feel. It’s made for those who like a challenge and those who want to break in a heavyweight pair and watch it evolve.

Our medium/high rise slim cut jeans made from our brand new 14oz broken twill selvedge denim. Broken twill denim was first used in 1964 by Wrangler as a solution for combatting leg twist. The process of weaving fabric in this method sees the combination of both right hand twill (RHT) and left hand twill (LHT) reversed every two warp ends, forming a zigzag-like pattern in the denim and resulting in no bias in either direction of the weave, therefore eliminating leg twist.

Based on the classic Levi’s 501 from 1955, this cut provides a similar fit to our relaxed tapered 888 style, with a more traditional silhouette. This means that — just like the highly coveted vintage Levi’s that came before them — these jeans offer a relaxed yet flattering fit for most body types, seen here in our signature 21oz overdyed selvedge denim.
To create this darkened variation, we take a pair of standard IH-1955S jeans and steep the entire garment in black dye using a direct dyeing process. This stains the indigo denim and stitching, with the added bonus of removing all shrinkage from the fabric.
